The `allowed_modules` check uses the canonical `'cmdb'` / `'workflow'` keys so per-analyst module access controls work without further changes. Grid is now 20 cards in a 7-column layout = 2 full rows of 7 plus a final row of 6, more visually balanced than the previous 18 = 2 rows of 7 + row of 4. |
| 363 | Self-Service      | Fix         | **Submitting a ticket with an un-attached recording now blocks instead of silently dropping it.** First real test of #362 surfaced an easy-to-miss UX trap &mdash; after clicking Stop the user sees a preview with *Use this* / *Discard* buttons, but if they ignored those buttons and clicked Submit, the recording sat in JS memory as `recordedBlob` and was silently lost (the ticket posted with an empty `recording_ids` array). The recording was never uploaded, never claimed, never visible to the analyst. **Fix**: `handleSubmit()` now checks `recordedBlob !== null` at the top and short-circuits if there's an unclaimed blob &mdash; expands the panel back open (in case it was collapsed), `scrollIntoView`s it, and replaces the status line with a red-text instruction: *"Click **Use this** to attach the recording, or **Discard** to drop it &mdash; then submit again."* No silent loss possible; the user gets an unambiguous next action. `discardRecording()` now also clears the inline red colour/weight so the status returns to its normal "Ready" look when the next recording starts. |
| 361 | Tickets           | Fix         | **Browser autofill disabled on the Add/Edit user modal.** Without `autocomplete` hints, browsers were happy to suggest the *analyst's own* email / password into a form whose entire purpose is creating an *end user* &mdash; a recipe for accidentally typing one's own credentials into someone else's record. Set `autocomplete="off"` on the form and on each text/email input, and `autocomplete="new-password"` on the password input (Chrome ignores `off` on password fields by design, but respects `new-password` as the signal that this is account creation, not a login). |
| 360 | Tickets           | Fix         | **Add/Edit user modal title no longer indented.** Follow-up to #359 &mdash; once `.modal-content` was given 30px padding, the modal-header's own default `padding: 20px 24px` from `inbox.css` stacked on top and the *Add user* title appeared indented from the left edge of the form fields below it. The settings page strips this for the same reason (`padding: 0; border-bottom: none; margin-bottom: 20px`); did the same here, scoped to `#userModal .modal-header`. |
| 359 | Tickets           | Fix         | **Add/Edit user modal now compact and padded like the analyst modal.** The new user CRUD modal from #358 was rendering at 900px wide with zero internal padding because `tickets/users.php` was inheriting the default `.modal-content` rule from `inbox.css` (designed for the wide content modals like the mailbox config dialog). The analyst modal in `tickets/settings/` looks right because that page ships a page-level `.modal-content { padding: 30px; max-width: 500px; }` override. Added the same override here, but scoped to `#userModal .modal-content` so it only applies to this modal and can't accidentally restyle anything else added later on the same page. |
| 355 | Workflows         | Fix         | **Ticket dispatches now carry the full current ticket state, and *Test fire* builds a synthetic payload from the workflow's own conditions.** Two bugs in #354 surfaced the moment a real workflow ran: **(1)** the `ticket.assigned` dispatch payload was `{ticket: {id}, analyst_id, team_id}` &mdash; only the ticket's id, not its other fields &mdash; so a perfectly reasonable condition like *priority is Critical* read `null` from `ticket.priority_id` and the engine correctly marked the run *skipped*. Same shape problem affected `ticket.status_changed` / `ticket.priority_changed` &mdash; each only carried a couple of sibling fields beyond the changed one. **Fix:** `api/tickets/assign_ticket.php` now reads back the FULL post-update ticket row once (id, subject, priority_id, status_id, department_id, type_id, assigned_analyst_id, owner_id, origin_id, created_by, plus requester_email joined from `users`) and includes that canonical `ticket` payload in every dispatch &mdash; so any condition on any ticket field works regardless of which trigger fired. Engine `availableFields()` widened to match: every `ticket.*` trigger's field hints now lists the full ticket field set plus the event-specific extras (old_/new_ ids, analyst_id, team_id), reused from a single `$fullTicket` array so they can't drift apart. **(2)** *Test fire* in the editor sent `payload: {}` (empty), which meant any workflow with any condition would always report *skipped* &mdash; the button was misleading users into thinking their workflow was broken when actually the test harness was broken. **Fix:** new `buildTestFirePayload()` in `workflow-editor.js` synthesises a payload from the workflow's own conditions: equality ops get `payload[field] = value` (first item if it's a list), inequality ops get a sentinel that won't match, contains gets the value embedded in a longer string, gt/lt get value&plusmn;1, is_empty/is_not_empty get `""`/`"x"`. Result: Test fire now means *"do my actions run when conditions pass"* &mdash; the workflow's conditions all trivially pass against the synthetic payload, so the action path actually executes and the user sees a real success/failed status. `workflow-editor.js` &rarr; `?v=7`. |
| 350 | Tickets           | Fix         | **You can now assign / change a ticket's priority from the open-ticket toolbar.** Priority could only be set at creation time (from the new-ticket modal), with no UI for changing it on an existing ticket &mdash; the detail-panel toolbar had Department, Type, Status, Origin, First Time Fix, IT Training, Owner, but no Priority dropdown. Added a Priority `<select>` to the toolbar between Status and Origin, sourced from the `ticket_priorities` lookup (active-only, ordered by display_order). Blank option lets you clear the priority (it's nullable). `assignPriority()` posts to `assign_ticket.php` and logs the change to the audit trail; the SLA engine is compute-on-read so it recomputes lazily on the next ticket fetch &mdash; no explicit recompute call needed. Backend changes: `api/tickets/assign_ticket.php` now accepts `priority_id` (null clears), `api/tickets/get_email_detail.php` returns `t.priority_id` alongside the existing `tp.name AS priority` so the dropdown can pre-select the current value. New `loadTicketPriorities()` runs at init, mirroring the existing `loadTicketStatuses` / `loadTicketTypes` pattern, with results filtered to `is_active`. `inbox.js` &rarr; `?v=24`. |
| 349 | System            | Fix         | **Waffle-menu fix: Workflows icon was missing its background colour; grid now four columns wide.** Two related tweaks to the waffle menu that drops down from the top-left of every module page. (1) The Workflows module was registered in the menu's `$modules` array (since #340) but never added to `includes/module-colors.php`'s `$defaultModuleColors` map, so the waffle's per-module gradient rule (`.waffle-module-icon.<key>`) had no entry for it &mdash; the icon rendered with no background and the SVG was an invisible white glyph on white. Added `'workflow' =&gt; ['#ea580c', '#c2410c']` (Tailwind orange-600 to orange-700) &mdash; distinct enough from contracts' amber to be tellable apart in the icon grid while staying in the same "automation" colour family. (2) `.waffle-modules` grid changed from `repeat(3, 1fr)` to `repeat(4, 1fr)` so the 20 modules render as a 4&times;5 grid instead of 3&times;7 &mdash; less scrolling, more glanceable. `.waffle-panel min-width` bumped from 360px to 460px so the 4-column grid has breathing room for the icon + label per cell. |
| 347 | Workflows         | Fix         | **Multi-select for lookup-field conditions is now the default, not hidden behind a deliberate operator switch.** Follow-up to #346 &mdash; the multi-select capability was there, but the user had to discover that flipping the operator dropdown from *equals* to *is one of* unlocked it, which is the kind of secret-handshake UX that absolutely nobody finds. The condition panel now always shows a checkbox list for lookup fields (priority / status / department / type / analyst / team / etc.) regardless of operator, and the operator dropdown for lookup fields is collapsed down to just **is**, **is not**, **is empty**, **is not empty** &mdash; mapping internally to `in` / `not_in` / `is_empty` / `is_not_empty`. Tick one box for an exact match (the engine treats `in` with a 1-item array identically to `equals`), tick several for OR semantics. Legacy `equals` / `not_equals` conditions on lookup fields get silently upgraded to `in` / `not_in` the first time the user opens them so the rebuilt UI stays consistent &mdash; behaviour preserved because the engine handles both. Free-text fields still get the full operator catalogue (contains, gt, lt, etc.). The op dropdown auto-rebuilds when the field changes, so flipping between a lookup and a free-text field instantly swaps the available operators. `workflow-editor.js` &rarr; `?v=5`. |
| 345 | Workflows         | Fix         | **Workflow editor lets you save in-progress drafts without at least one action.** The original Save flow blocked client-side AND server-side with *"At least one action is required"*, but that's actively unhelpful while building a workflow step-by-step (pick a trigger &rarr; add conditions &rarr; <em>and now you can't save your progress until you stub an action</em>). The engine itself tolerates zero actions &mdash; the action loop just doesn't run, and the execution row is logged as a normal success/skipped run with an empty step log &mdash; so the only thing the strict gate enforced was the friction. Removed the check in `assets/js/workflow-editor.js` `save()` and the mirror in `api/workflow/save.php`; on a successful save with zero actions the user gets a soft *info* toast (*"Saved — but this workflow has no actions yet, so it won't do anything until you add one"*) instead of being blocked. New i18n key `workflow.toast.saved_no_actions`. `workflow-editor.js` &rarr; `?v=3`. |
| 344 | Workflows         | Fix         | **AI Test button respects the global `SSL_VERIFY_PEER` kill switch from `config.php`.** Dev installs without a CA bundle wired into php.ini run with `SSL_VERIFY_PEER = false` so every outbound HTTPS skips peer verification &mdash; but the workflow AI Test / compose calls were ignoring it and only honouring the per-form Verify SSL toggle on the settings page. Testing an Anthropic / OpenAI key on a dev install therefore failed with `Failed: Network error: SSL certificate problem: unable to get local issuer certificate`. Added a tiny helper `workflowEffectiveSslVerify(bool $perCallVerify): bool` in `api/workflow/_ai_helpers.php` that ANDs the global constant with the per-form toggle, and routed all four curl call sites &mdash; `wfCallAnthropic` + `wfCallOpenAI` in `_ai_helpers.php` and `wfTestAnthropic` + `wfTestOpenAI` in `test_ai_key.php` &mdash; through it. The per-form toggle still works as before for production installs where the global is true (e.g. corporate inspecting proxy with a self-signed cert needs to opt out of verification for one integration without disabling globally). The same fix in the RFP module's curl drivers is a separate pre-existing bug not in scope here. |
| 339 | Process Mapper    | Fix         | **Collapsed left panel was leaking the left edges of its contents through the 16px hot-zone.** The "Show on hover" sidebar mode (#338) clips the sidebar to a 16px strip via `overflow: hidden`, but the children (the "+ New" button, the search box, the process list) were still rendered &mdash; you could see a thin slice of each control peeking out of the strip, which looked unfinished. Added a `.pm-layout.sidebar-hover .pm-sidebar > *` rule that sets `opacity: 0; pointer-events: none` on the direct children of the collapsed sidebar; on `:hover` they fade back in (`opacity: 1`) with an `0.08s` transition delay so they don't appear over a half-expanded strip mid-slide. The vertical strip indicator (`::before` pseudo-element) is unaffected by the `>` selector, so the hoverability hint stays visible. `process-mapper.css` &rarr; `?v=10`. |
| 337 | Process Mapper    | Fix         | **URL badge was invisible on diamond / hexagon / trapezoid / cloud steps and hung in empty space outside circle / pill steps.** The badge was positioned at `top: 4px; right: 4px;` (bbox top-right corner) which works for rectangular shapes, but the bounding-box top-right falls outside the visible region for several others. For clip-path shapes (diamond, hexagon, trapezoid, cloud) `clip-path` clips descendants too &mdash; the badge was being clipped away entirely. For border-radius shapes (circle, pill) the badge wasn't clipped, but it floated in transparent space outside the coloured fill, looking detached from the step. Added per-shape `[data-shape="..."] .pm-step-url-badge` positioning rules that pull the badge inward into a spot that's reliably inside the visible region across the default size range &mdash; diamond at `top: 26%; right: 30%;` (inside the polygon's top-right slope), hexagon / trapezoid at `top: 6px; right: 28%;` (inside the flat top edge), cloud at `top: 18%; right: 22%;` (inside the middle ellipse), circle at `top: 14%; right: 18%;` (inside the top-right arc), pill at `top: 6px; right: 32px;` (past the right rounded end-cap). `process-mapper.css` &rarr; `?v=8`. |
| 332 | Process Mapper    | Fix         | **PNG / PDF export was clipping content reachable only by scrolling sideways.** `.pm-canvas` is a scroll container (`overflow: auto`), and `html2canvas` uses the element's CSS box as its rendering bounds &mdash; so any step sitting beyond the visible viewport was being chopped off the export even though the bounding-box rect we passed in clearly extended past it. Fixed by temporarily expanding the canvas during capture: in `captureCanvas()`, before calling `html2canvas`, the canvas is given an explicit `width`/`height` equal to `max(scrollWidth, rect.x + rect.width)` × `max(scrollHeight, rect.y + rect.height)`, switched to `overflow: visible`, and pulled out of its parent's flex layout with `flex: 0 0 auto`. The connector SVG layer is pinned to the same expanded dimensions because some browsers compute its `width: 100%` from the scroll viewport rather than the new box. All four properties (plus the SVG attrs and the scroll position) are stashed before mutation and restored in the `finally` block so a thrown exception can't leave the canvas mis-sized. `.pm-canvas-wrap` already has `overflow: hidden` so the user doesn't see the canvas balloon during the ~half-second capture. `process-mapper.js` &rarr; `?v=7`. |
| 313 | Tasks             | Fix         | **Tasks module pages now cache-bust their CSS/JS** with `?v=` query strings on `tasks.css`, `tasks.js`, `tasks-calendar.js` and `tasks-timeline.js` (board, calendar, timeline and settings pages). The tasks module was the only one without cache-busting, so JS/CSS changes &mdash; such as the new Start Date field in the detail panel &mdash; would not appear until users manually hard-refreshed. |
| 315 | Tasks             | Fix         | **Stray main-window scrollbar on the Tasks board, calendar and timeline.** `tasks.css` set the `body` to `overflow:auto` and `.tasks-container` to `height:calc(100vh - 50px)`, which assumed a 50px-tall header &mdash; but the real header has no fixed height and renders ~56px (`padding:12px 20px`), so header + container overflowed the viewport by a few pixels and the browser added a vertical scrollbar. Replaced the hardcoded maths with a proper flex layout: `body` is `height:100vh; overflow:hidden; display:flex; flex-direction:column`, the header is `flex-shrink:0`, and `.tasks-container` is `flex:1; min-height:0` &mdash; so the content fills the viewport exactly regardless of header height, with no clipping and no stray scrollbar. The settings page (which legitimately scrolls) re-asserts `display:block` in its own stylesheet. `tasks.css` bumped to `?v=4`. |
| 317 | Tasks             | Fix         | **Drag-reorder drop indicator invisible in scrolling board columns.** The purple line that shows where a dragged card will land vanished whenever its column had enough cards to scroll. Cause: `.board-cards` is a `flex-direction:column` container and the `.drop-indicator` is an empty `<div>` &mdash; so its min-content height is 0, and when the column overflowed, flexbox's `flex-shrink` compressed the indicator to 0px (the cards resist because their text gives them a min-content height; the empty indicator does not). Fixed by adding `flex-shrink:0` to `.drop-indicator` (and to `.task-card` for good measure, so cards can never be squished either). `tasks.css` bumped to `?v=6`. |

Execution is synchronous within a single PHP request, so `WorkflowEngine::run()` is now a thin guard wrapper around the real body (renamed `runInner()`) backed by three request-scoped counters: **(1) an active-workflow stack** &mdash; a workflow already executing in the current chain is refused re-entry, which catches *every* cycle since a cycle must revisit a workflow still on the stack; **(2) `MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH` (10)** &mdash; a hard nesting-depth ceiling as a backstop for an absurdly deep but acyclic cascade; **(3) `MAX_RUNS_PER_REQUEST` (100)** &mdash; a per-request total-run ceiling as a backstop for fan-out blow-ups where each run spawns new, distinct workflows. The stack-pop and depth-decrement run in a `finally` so one throwing run can't wedge the counters for the rest of the request. A blocked run is **still recorded** &mdash; new `recordAbortedRun()` writes a `workflow_executions` row with a new **`aborted`** status, a `loop_protection` step-log entry, and a human-readable reason, and stamps the parent workflow's `last_run_status = 'aborted'` (without bumping `run_count`, since nothing actually executed) so the block is visible in the audit. Canonical fields (`task.id` / `task.title` / `task.priority_id` / `task.assignee_id`) are read back from the row since a kanban drag may only send `status`. **(3) `change.approved`** &mdash; fired from **both** approval routes: `api/change-management/submit_cab_vote.php` dispatches when a CAB vote tips the change over its approval threshold (the existing change SELECT was widened to also read `title` / `risk_level` / `approver_id`), and `api/change-management/save.php` dispatches when a manual status edit moves the change into Approved (guarded on the old status not already being Approved, so re-saving doesn't re-fire). | 442 | Forms             | Feature     | **Real form versioning &mdash; Save updates in place, Save as new version snapshots, Versions dropdown browses history.** Before: every regular Save bumped `version_number` with no actual snapshot, so "v3" was a counter not a thing you could revert to. After: a version *is* its own row in the chain. **Schema**: `forms.parent_form_id INT NULL` added &mdash; each row points back at its predecessor; the leaf (no children) is the editable current version, older rows are frozen. **`save_form.php`** no longer bumps `version_number`; just refreshes `modified_by/date`. Server-side check rejects in-place saves to non-leaf rows so a stale tab can't mutate history. **New APIs**: `create_version.php` (clones the current form + every `form_fields` row into a new chain entry whose `version_number = source + 1`; refuses to fork from a non-leaf) and `list_versions.php` (walks the chain back to root then forward, returns ordered rows with `is_current` flag &mdash; mirrors network-mapper's `list_versions.php` shape). `get_form.php` now returns `parent_form_id`, `version_number`, and an `is_leaf` boolean so the editor knows whether to enable Save. **Editor UI**: new toolbar v-pill (clickable; opens the Properties drawer), new Versions dropdown (lists the chain with the current row badged green; click any row to navigate to that version), new *Save as new version* button (offers to save in-progress changes first, then forks). When viewing a non-leaf row: orange read-only banner appears, Save is disabled with a tooltip explaining how to fork from the current version. **Two bugs fixed while in there**: (1) `saveForm()` now returns a success boolean so `createNewVersion()` can chain a save-before-fork. (2) The save payload only sent `options` for `dropdown` fields &mdash; the new `radio` / `checkboxes` types from #441 were losing their options on save. For a vanilla install with the seeded Green/Amber/Red labels, 100% of historical rows backfill cleanly &mdash; zero orphans, no admin action needed. **Reads are now joined**: `get_todays_checks.php` LEFT JOINs the statuses table for label/colour/requires-notes (with an `IsOrphan` flag when StatusID is NULL but the Status snapshot is set); `get_chart_data.php` INNER JOINs on `StatusID` and groups by it (orphans excluded from the chart until remapped). **Writes carry the FK**: `save_check_result.php` now takes `statusId` instead of `status` (the dashboard sends the StatusID from the button it clicked), validates against the table, writes `StatusID` and sets `Status = NULL`. The dashboard's notes-modal hidden input changed from `modalStatusValue` to `modalStatusId`. **Deletes preserve labels for orphans**: `delete_status.php` now snapshots the about-to-be-deleted Label into `morningChecks_Results.Status` for any referencing row before deleting, all in one transaction &mdash; the FK SET NULL clears `StatusID` but the label survives so the normalisation tool can show what the orphan used to be. **Two new APIs**: `get_status_orphans.php` (distinct orphan labels with row counts &mdash; drives both the dashboard banner and the settings tool) and `normalise_status.php` (transactional bulk-map `{label, statusId}` pairs to set `StatusID` and clear `Status` on all matching orphan rows). **Dashboard**: shows a yellow warning banner with a link to Settings → Statuses when any orphans exist; per-row orphan badge in the status column when a check's most recent result is orphaned. **Settings → Statuses tab**: new highlighted normalisation section appears beneath the statuses table only when orphans exist &mdash; one row per distinct orphan label with count + a dropdown of active statuses + per-row *Map* button + *Map all* shortcut. **Cleanup**: `save_status.php`'s former rename-cascade `UPDATE morningChecks_Results SET Status = ? WHERE Status = ?` is gone (with the JOIN at read time, label changes propagate automatically; the old cascade would have wrongly claimed orphan rows that happened to share the old label). |

Chart-footer's `min-height: 40px` keeps the chevron visible at the end of the slide. **Two gotchas handled in JS**: (1) the inline `style.height` set by `applyChartHeightFromPct` would beat the collapsed class's `height: 0`, so the rule uses `!important` &mdash; the only reasonable place to use it given inline styles always win otherwise. (2) On expand, we update the target inline height first (so the transition has a valid end value if the window was resized while collapsed) but skip the immediate `chartInstance.resize()` call &mdash; the canvas parent is still 0px tall when the call would fire. | 398 | Change management | Improvement | **Change form pairs half-width fields automatically &mdash; dropdowns and short inputs go 2-per-row, textareas / composites take the full row.** Follow-up to #397. Width is fixed per field type (dropdowns + datetime pickers + short text are `half`; textareas, composite widgets like CAB and risk-scoring, and headline fields like *Title* are `full`) so moving a field to a different section keeps its width. **Rendering**: `refreshFormLayout()` stamps `data-width` onto each `.cm-field-wrap` after positioning it; the change-management CSS turns `.cm-form-section` into a `display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap` row, with `half` wraps sized at `calc(50% - 10px)` and `full` wraps at 100% &mdash; pairing emerges automatically from layout order, no per-row container needed. **Orphan handling**: a `half` field whose neighbour isn't also `half` (i.e. it's between two fulls, or trailing at the end of a section) would leave awkward whitespace next to it. JS walks each section after placement and adds `.cm-field-half-orphan` to those, which stretches them back to full width. Determined by **adjacency in display order**, so reordering in Form Fields settings is what controls the pairing &mdash; admins can put two halves next to each other to pair them, or place a full between two halves to break them apart. **Also**: APIs (`get_field_layout`, `save_field_layout`) now return `width` alongside `label` per field; first-visible section gets a `.cm-form-section--first` class so its heading drops the top border / padding regardless of which section ended up first after reordering (replaces the old hardcoded inline `style="margin-top:0;..."` on the General-info heading); removed the matching dead inline style from `change-management/index.php`. Sweep of `api/` &mdash; **435 endpoints** changed from `session_start()` to `session_start(['read_and_close' => true])`, so any page firing concurrent AJAX (dashboards, asset table view, every settings page, the tickets inbox folder loads, the calendar, the rota, the help pages' embedded charts, etc.) now runs those requests in actual parallel instead of queueing behind PHP's default exclusive `flock` on the session file. **Skipped (deliberately)**: 9 files that mutate `$_SESSION` mid-request and need the lock to write safely &mdash; the analyst-side MFA + password-change flow (`api/myaccount/change_password.php`, `setup_mfa.php`, `verify_login_otp.php`, `verify_mfa.php`), the self-service portal auth flow (`api/self-service/login.php`, `register.php`, `update_profile.php`, `verify_login_otp.php`), and `api/system/save_analyst_modules.php`. Identification was mechanical &mdash; grep for `$_SESSION[...] = ` / `session_destroy` / `session_regenerate` / `session_unset` / `unset($_SESSION` &mdash; so anything not in that list was treated as read-only and safe to flip. Mechanism: `read_and_close` opens the session, populates `$_SESSION` for the auth-check (still works because the read happened before the close), then releases the file lock so subsequent requests in the same browser tab don't queue. Single-line change per file, no behavioural diffs for non-auth endpoints. |

| 308 | Tickets           | Fix         | **SLA help page Example 2 (Estonia cross-timezone) options shown inconsistent margins**. User-caught: Options A and B both landed the SLA at the literal wire (consumption = target exactly), while Option C showed 30 min margin &mdash; making C look unfairly generous in comparison when really all three meet the SLA at the same level. Fix is consistent: bumped the raise time from 16:00 UK Friday to 16:30 UK Friday throughout the scenario, then picked reply times in each option that consume exactly 30 min of the 60 min target. **Option A (UK calendar)**: 30 min consumed Friday 16:30-17:00 UK, paused weekend, Estonia analyst replies 10:00 Estonia Mon (= 08:00 UK while UK calendar still paused) &mdash; consumption stays at 30 min, met with 30 min margin. Added a "any reply after 09:30 UK / 11:30 Estonia would breach" line to make the wire visible. **Option B (Estonia calendar)**: ticket arrives 18:30 Estonia Friday (after Estonia close), clock starts Mon 09:00 Estonia, analyst replies 09:30 Estonia (= 07:30 UK), 30 min consumed, met with 30 min margin. The wall-clock-vs-SLA gap is still in the prose (UK customer raised 16:30 Friday UK, replied 07:30 UK Monday). **Option C (overlap calendar)**: ticket raised 16:30 UK Friday (outside the overlap which closes 15:00 UK), reply at 11:30 Estonia Monday (= 09:30 UK, 30 min into the overlap reopening), 30 min consumed, met with 30 min margin. All three now show the same outcome with the same margin, so readers can compare the *qualitative* differences (who feels the pressure, who waits how long wall-clock) rather than being misled by quantitative artefacts of arbitrary example times. Four-paragraph edit; no schema or behaviour change. |
| 307 | Tickets           | Fix         | **SLA help page Example 1 maths wrong**. User caught a self-inflicted bug in the worked example I shipped in #306. Ticket raised Wed 16:30 with a 1h response target on a Mon-Fri 09:00-17:00 calendar: 30 min consumed Wed 16:30-17:00 + 30 min consumed Thu 09:00-09:30 = exactly 60 min = at the wire, not "with 30 min to spare". And a reply at Thu 10:00 would consume 30 + 60 = 90 min = 150% / breached by 30 min, not "exactly 100%". Kept the times (Thu 09:30 and Thu 10:00) and fixed the prose to match the correct maths &mdash; the breach scenario at Thu 10:00 is actually more useful for teaching than the "comfortable margin" version because it illustrates the easy-to-miss trap where an analyst arriving at 09:00 assumes they have the full hour, when 30 min has already been consumed the previous evening. Single-paragraph edit, no other changes. |

| 303 | Watchtower        | Feature     | **"Tickets paused too long" guardrail on the Watchtower dashboard**. Crossover between the Tickets/SLA pause-the-clock feature (#295/#298) and Watchtower's at-a-glance attention model. Catches the well-known ITIL antipattern of analysts parking tickets in "On Hold" / "Awaiting Vendor" to escape the SLA clock when they're stuck or busy &mdash; tickets sit indefinitely with the SLA showing as paused, customer experience suffers, but reporting looks fine because the SLA metric isn't tripping. Now the Tickets card on Watchtower shows an amber attention row whenever there are tickets currently in a paused-SLA status (any status with `pauses_sla = 1`) where the last status change was longer ago than the configured threshold (wall-clock hours). Anchor for "how long has it been paused" is the latest `ticket_audit` row with `field_name = 'status'`; falls back to `tickets.created_datetime` if no status-change row exists (e.g. ticket has never moved off its default status). Single SQL query, no per-row PHP work &mdash; uses a correlated subquery joined to the audit table so it scales to thousands of tickets. | 301 | Tickets           | Improvement | **Rate limiting + per-run logging on the SLA breach-check cron**. Two follow-ups to #299 the user asked for. **(1) Rate limiting** &mdash; three layers, the first two HTTP-only, the third applied to CLI + HTTP equally: (a) the existing shared-secret token check (#299); (b) **per-IP failed-auth lockout** &mdash; >10 wrong-token attempts from the same IP in the past hour returns 429 for a full hour, defeating brute-force probing without needing fail2ban or similar; (c) **min interval between successful runs** &mdash; `sla_cron_min_interval_seconds` setting (default 30s, configurable in `system_settings`); even a valid-token request gets a 429 if it arrives sooner than that after the last successful run. Catches accidental double-scheduling, runaway loops, and post-token-leak abuse without affecting any reasonable schedule (5-min crons sit comfortably above 30s). **(2) Per-run logging** &mdash; new **`sla_cron_runs`** table with one row per invocation: `started_at` / `ended_at` / `duration_ms` / `invocation` (cli|http) / `client_ip` / `outcome` (ok / rate_limited / auth_failed / config_missing / error) / `sent_count` / `skipped_count` / `error_count` / `notes`. Indexed on `started_at` and `(client_ip, started_at)` so the rate-limit lookups stay O(log n). Logs both accepted *and* rejected runs &mdash; same source of truth for the rate-limit check + a security audit (you can see exactly when someone hit you with the wrong token and from where). Rows pruned automatically at the end of every run based on `sla_cron_log_retention_days` (default 30 days, configurable). Net effect was `<button class="add-btn" onclick="..."<?php echo ... ?></button>`, which leaves the opening tag malformed: PHP runs and emits the translated text, but the browser sees an unclosed-attribute mess and the button doesn't render as a clickable button at all (collapsing into the surrounding HTML). Same bug in 9 button-text patterns &mdash; the 4 bulk replaces (Add ×11, Save ×6, Cancel ×6, Close ×2) and 5 per-instance swaps (Logs, Check All, Test connection, Verify, Reset Password). Fix: replace_all again with `'<?php echo ... ?></button>'` → `'><?php echo ... ?></button>'` so the opening tag's closing `>` is restored. PHP lint clean. JS pagination Prev/Next swaps from the same PR were never affected because their old_string already included `">` which was preserved. The mistake would have been visible immediately in any browser smoke-test of the page &mdash; lesson: when bulk-replacing across tag boundaries, double-check the `<` and `>` are still balanced in the new string. |

Ed's screenshot of MFG-151-13903 showed the "Did you find this email helpful?" grey box visually floating *over* the Time Entries section &mdash; a textbook positioning-escape symptom, not a tag-balance one. Two targeted fixes: **JS** &mdash; `safeEmailHtml()` now also strips `<style>`, `<script>`, `<link>`, `<base>`, `<meta>` tags from the parsed document before returning the serialised body. DOMParser already does this in a separate document context, so the stripped tags never touch the live DOM. **CSS** &mdash; `.email-body-content` and `.thread-message-body` get `contain: layout paint` (creates a containing block so absolutely-positioned descendants are positioned relative to the email box, not the page; clips painting at the box boundary) plus `overflow: hidden` (belt-and-braces for any layout-overflow that doesn't trigger `contain: paint`'s clipping). Together: HTML can't bleed (tag balance), CSS can't bleed (`<style>` stripped), and positioning can't bleed (containing block + paint clip). | 282 | Tickets           | Fix         | **Malformed email bodies (unclosed tags) swallowed the CMDB / time-entries / notes panels below them**. Reported via ticket MFG-151-13903 where the email body ran straight into the operational sections at the bottom of the reading pane. Root cause: email HTML was interpolated raw into the reading pane via template literals (`<div class="email-body-content">${email.body_content}</div>` and the same for thread messages). When that HTML contains an unclosed tag &mdash; a `<div>` with no closing `</div>`, an open `<font>` running to end-of-message, half a `<table>` &mdash; the browser's HTML parser balances the unclosed tag at the end of its *parent* element rather than at the end of the email body. Net effect: the sibling containers that followed (`#cmdbObjectsContainer`, `#timeEntriesContainer`, `#notesContainer`) silently ended up nested *inside* the email body's runaway element, with all the visual chaos that implies. Server-side processing in `get_email_detail.php` only strips control characters; nothing balances tags. Fix is a one-helper `safeEmailHtml(html)` function in `inbox.js` that runs the email body through `DOMParser.parseFromString(html, 'text/html')` and returns `doc.body.innerHTML`. DOMParser invokes the same battle-tested HTML parser the browser uses for full page loads &mdash; it auto-balances any unclosed tags as it builds the parsed document's body, so the serialised output is well-formed and cannot bleed into sibling elements when assigned via innerHTML. Bonus security property: scripts in the parsed document don't execute (documented behaviour of DOMParser for `text/html`). Applied at both injection sites &mdash; the single-email body (`renderTicket`) and each message in the conversation thread (`loadCorrespondenceThread`). No CSS or DOM-structure changes needed because the tag balancing happens *before* the HTML hits the live DOM, which is the only point at which the bleed can actually occur. Cache buster bumped to `inbox.js?v=19`. |

| 231 | Process Mapper    | Fix         | **Lane divider drag now actually moves the contents below**. Previously the divider followed the cursor pixel-by-pixel but each per-frame `delta` (often 1px) got eaten by `snap()` when applied to step positions — `snap(200 + 1) = 200` — so contents never moved no matter how far the divider was dragged. The divider visually drifted away from anything below it, leaving items glued at their original `y`. Fix: snap `targetH` to the grid in the resize mousemove handler (`const targetH = Math.max(80, snap(laneDragging.startHeight + dy))`), so lane heights now change in 20px increments matching the step grid. With grid-aligned deltas, the shift in `resizeLaneTo` applies cleanly: contents move 20px each time the divider crosses a grid line. Drag feels "snappy" in the same way step drag already does — consistent across the whole UI. Detail panel's Height input intentionally left unsnapped so typed values are respected for fine-tuning. |
| 230 | Process Mapper    | Fix         | **Resizing a lane now physically moves everything below the divider** with it (lanes, steps, groups). Previously the resize shifted steps in lanes below based on `step.lane_id` matching, so any step with a missing or stale `lane_id` (e.g. one placed before its lane was tagged) would stay anchored at its old `y` while its lane band shifted underneath it — leaving the step "stranded" in the wrong lane and creating confusion about which lane it belonged to. Fix swaps the criterion from `lane_id` matching to **visual centre position vs the resized lane's bottom edge** (matching how groups already worked), so anything visually below the divider moves by the same delta the divider moved. Stale `lane_id` values are not re-tagged inside the resize — that's left to the existing auto-tag pass at the start of the next lane drag, which keeps the lane logic itself untouched. |

So if you were editing a step/group/lane's properties, the panel would slide closed every 2 seconds and you'd have to re-click the thing to keep going. Fix has two parts: (1) `openProcess()` gains a `preserveDetail` parameter; `save()` passes `true`, sidebar process-click still passes the default `false` so switching processes still closes the panel cleanly. (2) `save()` captures the current selection by **stable identity** (step's `{x, y}`, group's `{x, y, width, height}`, lane's `display_order`) *before* the save runs, then after `openProcess(newId, true)` reloads the data with fresh real IDs, re-finds the equivalent entity and calls `showDetailForStep/Group/Lane()` to re-populate the panel with the new IDs. Position-based matching is robust because positions are saved as part of the same payload, so the reloaded data has the same coords. If the entity can't be found after reload (e.g. it was deleted in the meantime), the panel closes gracefully. Multi-step selections (size > 1) aren't preserved — the panel only shows single-entity details anyway. |

No data model change needed; the lane derivation is purely runtime, so groups remain free-form and can still be moved across lane boundaries or out of lanes entirely. |

New `autoAssignAllStepLanes()` helper scans every step and stamps its `lane_id` based on whichever lane its vertical centre currently sits in; called at the start of every lane drag (header or divider) so the upcoming reorder/resize math operates on a fully-tagged step set. Also fixed a secondary arithmetic bug in the reorder-trigger loop: when iterating lanes to find which slot the cursor is over, the dragged lane's height was being skipped from the running `acc` because of an early-`continue`, so non-dragged lane midlines were computed without accounting for the dragged lane's still-occupied visual space. Result: the swap fired too eagerly (cursor only needed to cross y=90 instead of y=270 in a 2-lane test). Loop now accumulates `acc` unconditionally and only skips the *test* against the cursor when iterating the dragged lane itself. |

Fix: removed `E_STRICT` from the severity lookup (added a broader handful of stable constants instead, all comment-documented), and now `chdir(dirname($importPath))` before the include then restore CWD after so the relative includes resolve correctly.
